Fremont County District Court: Location, Hours, Contact Info, and Services

The Fremont County District Court is a vital part of Colorado’s judicial system, serving Fremont County with jurisdiction over felony criminal cases, major civil disputes, family law matters, and probate cases. This guide provides essential information about the court’s location, hours, contact details, and services to help you navigate its processes effectively.

Fremont County District Court Location and Contact Information

  • Address: 136 Justice Center Road, Canon City, CO 81212
  • Google Maps: Fremont County District Court Location
  • Phone: 719-269-0100
  • Fax: 719-204-2275
  • Website: Fremont County District Court Official Website

Court Hours

  • Monday to Friday: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  • Saturday and Sunday: Closed

Overview of Fremont County District Court

The Fremont County District Court is part of Colorado’s 11th Judicial District and handles:

  • Felony Criminal Cases: Murder, robbery, drug offenses, sex crimes, and more.
  • Civil Cases: Lawsuits exceeding $25,000, property disputes, and contract breaches.
  • Family Law: Divorce, child custody, paternity, and support cases.
  • Probate and Estate Matters: Wills, trusts, guardianships, and conservatorships.
  • Juvenile Cases: Crimes committed by minors and dependency issues.

Court Locations

The District Court operates primarily from the Fremont County Justice Center in Canon City but also holds sessions in other locations:

  • Canon City Courthouse: 136 Justice Center Road, Canon City, CO 81212
  • Florence Courthouse: 110 E Front St, Florence, CO 81226
  • Salida Courthouse: 448 E 1st St #109, Salida, CO 81201
  • Cripple Creek Courthouse: 334 E Carr Ave, Cripple Creek, CO 80813

Accessing Court Records

Court records can be accessed through:

  1. Online Portal: Search by case number, name, or date via the Colorado Courts Portal.
  2. In-Person: Visit the clerk’s office at the Canon City courthouse.
  3. Mail Request: Submit a written request with the required fees.

Note: Some records, such as juvenile and mental health cases, may be confidential and unavailable online.

Filing and Paying Fees

  • Filing Fees: Vary by case type; check the court’s website for details.
  • Payment Methods: Cash, check, money order, or credit/debit card (processing fees may apply).

Courtroom Procedures

  • Security Screening: All visitors must pass through metal detectors. Prohibited items include weapons, food, and drinks.
  • Courtroom Etiquette: Dress professionally, turn off electronic devices, and address the judge as “Your Honor.”

Jury Duty

If summoned for jury duty:

  • Selection Process: Potential jurors are screened for fairness.
  • Responsibilities: Attend all trial proceedings, deliberate on verdicts, and follow court rules.
  • Compensation: Jurors receive a daily stipend for their service.

Working with an Attorney

Hiring an attorney is highly recommended for District Court cases. Tips for finding legal representation:

  • Referrals: Ask for recommendations from trusted sources.
  • Research: Look for attorneys with experience in your case type.
  • Consultation: Discuss fees, strategy, and expectations before hiring.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

  1. How do I request court records?
    Use the online portal or visit the clerk’s office in person.
  2. What is the difference between District Court and County Court?
    District Court handles felonies and major civil cases, while County Court deals with misdemeanors and smaller claims.
  3. What should I wear to court?
    Dress professionally in business attire. Avoid shorts, tank tops, or ripped clothing.
  4. How do I find hearing dates?
    Check the online register of actions or contact the clerk’s office.
  5. Can I represent myself in court?
    Yes, but it’s advisable to hire an attorney for complex cases.

Conclusion

The Fremont County District Court plays a critical role in administering justice for serious criminal and civil matters in Fremont County. Whether you’re involved in a felony case, a major lawsuit, or a family law matter, understanding the court’s procedures and resources can help you navigate the legal system effectively. For further assistance, contact the court directly or consult with a qualified attorney.
